parts.label: (c)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: State a correct equation for the line through \(B\) and \(C\), e.g. \(\mathbf r=\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\mathbf k+\lambda(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)\) or \(\mathbf r=3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k+\mu(-2\mathbf i-\mathbf j-2\mathbf k)\). B1. Taking a general point of \(BC\) as \(P\), form an equation in \(\lambda\) by equating \(\overrightarrow{OP}\cdot\overrightarrow{BC}\) to zero, or by Pythagoras in triangle \(OBP\) or \(OCP\), or by setting the derivative of \(|OP|\) to zero. M1. Solve and obtain \(\lambda=-\frac59\). A1. Obtain \(\frac13\sqrt2\), or equivalent. A1. Alternative: use a scalar product to find projection \(CN\) or \(BN\) of \(OC\) or \(OB\) on \(BC\). M1. Obtain \(CN=\frac53\) or \(BN=\frac{14}{3}\). A1. Use Pythagoras to find \(ON\). M1. Obtain \(\frac13\sqrt2\), or equivalent. A1. Total [4].
